sections.title: Before & After Real Shifts

slots.text: These aren’t dramatic overnight transformations. They’re the quiet, profound changes that happen when someone finally stops running from themselves.
“I was a VP at 38, everyone thought I had it figured out. I was quietly having a panic attack every Sunday night before the work week.”
Negotiated a 4-day week, started therapy, began a side project she’d been “too busy” for. Sunday nights are now her favourite time of the week.
“I’d been in the same role for 7 years. I knew I needed to leave but I kept telling myself ‘not yet.’ Not yet became 5 years of not yet.”
Left his job, launched an independent consultancy, landed his first two clients within 60 days. Reports sleeping better than he has in a decade.
“My whole identity was ‘engineer at Google.’ When I got passed over for promotion I genuinely didn’t know who I was without that story.”
Rebuilt his sense of identity from the inside. Now leads a team he loves and has a life outside work for the first time in his adult life.
“I was making more money than I ever dreamed of and completely miserable. I was too ashamed to tell anyone — it felt ungrateful to be unhappy."
Gave herself permission to want something different. Now runs her own boutique, works 30 hours a week, & describes herself as “genuinely happy”.

sections.title: Answers to what most clients ask first

slots.text: Answers to what most clients ask first
Don't see your question? Reach out — we respond personally within one business day.
How does the coaching process work?

We begin with a free discovery call so we can assess fit and discuss what you're hoping to work on. From there, you'll choose a program, receive access to your dashboard, and book your first session. Sessions are held weekly or bi-weekly depending on your plan.
How do I book my sessions?
Sessions are booked directly through your AllCoach dashboard. Once you enroll, you’ll see an integrated calendar where you can select a time that works for you — no back-and-forth emails needed.

I hold an MA in Clinical Psychology and a Licensed Mental Health Counselor credential (LMHC). I’m also a Professional Certified Coach through the ICF and have completed specialized training in trauma-informed care and the Gottman Method. I’ve been in practice for 12 years with over 1,200 clients.
Do you offer sliding-scale or reduced fees?
I keep a small number of sliding-scale spots for clients who need them. Reach out before enrolling and we’ll talk about it honestly — cost shouldn’t be the reason you don’t begin.
Is this therapy or coaching — and what’s the difference?

Both. Therapy focuses on healing — understanding and processing past experiences, mental health, and emotional regulation. Coaching focuses on growth — goals, habits, accountability, and forward movement. My programs blend both intentionally, depending on what you need most.

slots.text: I built TherapyCoach because therapy should feel human

After twelve years in private clinical practice, I wanted to bring the depth of traditional therapy into a modern coaching format — guided, structured, and held with the same care I'd offer in my office.

images.subject: person
images.description: Smiling young woman in a gray blazer sitting by a window

sections.title: From clinical practice to coaching

slots.text: I began my career in a community mental health clinic in Brooklyn, where the days were long and the conversations were unguarded. I learned to listen, to slow down, and to trust that the body knows things the mind hasn’t named yet.

Over the years I moved into private practice, then into trauma-informed work, then into coaching. Each shift was an attempt to make depth work more accessible — to meet people earlier, before crisis, with practices they could actually use.
TherapyCoach is the culmination of that arc. A small set of carefully designed programs, supported by real one-on-one sessions, held inside an environment built for confidentiality and ease.
Awareness without practice fades. Practice without awareness exhausts.
The nervous system learns through repetition and safety — not insight alone.
Therapy works best when it includes the body, not only the story.
Healing is not a destination. It’s a relationship you build with yourself.
